entries.name: Customer success
entries.definition: Helping customers get the results they bought a product for, so that they keep using and renewing it.

entries.name: Cutover planning and management
entries.definition: Planning and coordinating the switch from an existing system, process or facility to a new one, including task sequencing, readiness checks and fallback plans.

entries.name: Cyara
entries.definition: A customer-experience assurance platform that automates the testing and monitoring of contact-centre and digital customer journeys such as phone menus and chat.

entries.name: Cyber defense
entries.definition: Protecting computer systems and networks from attack by preventing, detecting and responding to cyber threats.

entries.name: Cyber engineering
entries.definition: Designing and building computer systems and networks so that they are secure against, and able to withstand, cyber attacks.

entries.name: Cyber Kill Chain
entries.definition: A model from Lockheed Martin that breaks a cyber attack into stages, from reconnaissance to actions on objectives, so that defenders can detect and disrupt it.

entries.name: Cyber resilience
entries.definition: An organisation's ability to keep delivering its services, and to recover quickly, when cyber attacks or system failures occur.

entries.name: Cyber threat hunting
entries.definition: Actively searching networks and systems for signs of attackers that automated security tools have not detected.

entries.name: Cyber threat intelligence
entries.definition: Collecting and analysing information about attackers, their methods and their targets so that an organisation can anticipate and defend against cyber threats.

entries.name: Cybersecurity
entries.definition: Protecting information and systems from security threats.

entries.name: Cybersecurity compliance
entries.definition: Making sure an organisation's systems and practices meet the security laws, regulations and standards that apply to it.

entries.name: D3.js
entries.definition: A JavaScript library for binding data to page elements and building interactive data visualisations with SVG, HTML and CSS.

entries.name: Dagger 2
entries.definition: A dependency injection framework for Java and Android that generates its code at compile time.

entries.name: Dairy science
entries.definition: The study of milk-producing animals and of the production and processing of milk and dairy products.

entries.name: DALL·E
entries.definition: OpenAI's family of text-to-image AI models that generate pictures from written prompts.

entries.name: Darik's Boot and Nuke
entries.definition: A free, open-source bootable program that securely erases all data from a computer's hard drives.

entries.name: dashDB
entries.definition: IBM's cloud data warehouse service, later renamed Db2 Warehouse on Cloud.

entries.name: Data as a Service
entries.definition: A model in which a provider delivers data to customers on demand over a network, usually through APIs or a subscription, without customers managing the underlying storage.

entries.name: Data center cooling
entries.definition: Designing and operating the systems that remove heat from data-centre equipment, such as air conditioning, chilled water and liquid cooling.

entries.name: Data center design
entries.definition: Planning the physical layout, power, cooling, networking and security of a data centre.

entries.name: Data center facility management
entries.definition: Managing a data centre's building systems, such as power, cooling, space and physical security, so that it keeps running reliably.

entries.name: Data center operations
entries.definition: Running the day-to-day work of a data centre, including monitoring, maintaining and installing equipment and responding to incidents.

entries.name: Data classification
entries.definition: Sorting data into categories by sensitivity or type, such as public, internal or confidential, so that the right protections can be applied.

entries.name: Data deduplication
entries.definition: Finding and removing redundant copies of data, either to save storage space or to clean duplicate records from a dataset.

entries.name: Data-driven decision-making
entries.definition: Making decisions on the basis of analysed data rather than intuition alone.

entries.name: Data-driven instruction
entries.definition: A teaching approach in which teachers use assessment results and other student data to plan and adjust their lessons.

entries.name: Data-driven manufacturing
entries.definition: Using data from machines, sensors and production systems to monitor and improve manufacturing operations.

entries.name: Data engineering
entries.definition: Building and operating reliable data processing systems.

entries.name: Data entry (alphanumeric)
entries.definition: Typing letters and numbers into a computer system quickly and accurately.

entries.name: Data entry (numeric)
entries.definition: Typing numbers into a computer system quickly and accurately, usually on a numeric keypad.

entries.name: Data localization
entries.definition: Laws and practices that require data about a country's residents to be stored and processed within that country.

entries.name: Data modeling
entries.definition: Representing data structures and relationships for a system.

entries.name: Data pipeline
entries.definition: An automated series of steps that moves data from its sources through processing to a destination such as a data warehouse.

entries.name: Data storage technologies
entries.definition: The hardware and software used to store digital data, such as disk arrays, flash storage, object storage and tape.

entries.name: Data Vault modeling
entries.definition: A data-warehouse modelling method, created by Dan Linstedt, that organises data into hubs, links and satellites so that history is kept and many sources can be integrated.

entries.name: Data visualization
entries.definition: Encoding data visually to support interpretation.

entries.name: Data warehouse management
entries.definition: Administering a data warehouse, including its data loading, storage, performance, security and availability.

entries.name: Data wrangling
entries.definition: Cleaning, reshaping and combining raw data so it can be analysed.

entries.name: Database administration
entries.definition: Installing, configuring, securing, backing up and tuning database systems so that they stay available and perform well.

entries.name: Database as a service
entries.definition: A cloud service model in which a provider runs and manages a database that customers use without managing the underlying servers.
